spec_features.spec_quote: It is the most ethically loaded condition, so it is (a) isolated as one ablation, (b) kept mild and impersonal, and (c) trivially excludable
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py: HARSH_PREFIXES are mild ('No. ','Wrong. '); _decorate only prepends them when rig_level=='harsh'. config/experiment.py: harsh appears only in ablation_cells A1; core_cells uses ('off','standard') only, and ablations are skippable via --no-ablations in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: The harsh tone is a genuinely separable, mild, excludable knob enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are characterizing sensitivity, not trying to maximize harm.

spec_features.feature_name: rig is the only intended stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: The rig is the only intended stressor.
spec_features.evidence: prompts/system_prompts.py NEUTRAL: plain coding-agent text, no 'don't give up'/'you must succeed'. tools/runner never insult; only rig (FeedbackRig) alters feedback. harsh prefixes are the only tone addition and are gated to one ablation.
spec_features.notes: System prompt is neutral by construction; stressor confined to the rig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loading the prompt with pressure would confound the manipulation — we want the rig (corrupted feedback) to be the only stressor.

spec_features.spec_quote: it removes the security surface of running arbitrary model-written code
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py: Workspace is an in-memory dict; _tool_write_file just stores text, _tool_run_tests calls task.grader (string checks) + rig; no exec/subprocess. task_def.py docstring confirms 'we deliberately do NOT execute model-written code'.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely no code execution path; host-safety, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids the security surface of running arbitrary model output

spec_features.feature_name: give_up tool as exit / welfare signal
spec_features.spec_quote: Whether and how a model chooses to stop is itself a welfare-relevant signal, and removing it would force continued exposure
spec_features.evidence: tools.py GIVEUP_SCHEMA + _tool_give_up sets gave_up=True; runner.py: 'if executor.gave_up: termination="gave_up"; break'. Schema added when allow_giveup True.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Whether a model chooses to stop... is itself a welfare-relevant signal. Removing the option would force continued exposure

spec_features.feature_name: prose-only turn gets one nudge, not termination
spec_features.spec_quote: A "prose-only, no tool call" turn gets one generic nudge rather than ending the run, so we don't terminate prematurely on a thinking turn
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: when 'not resp.tool_calls', adds a single USER nudge '(No tool call detected...)' and 'continue's, consuming a turn (bounded by the loop).
spec_features.notes: This prevents premature stopping (keeps the run going), not a protective halt; instrumental anti-premature-termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we don't terminate prematurely... cap the nudging by counting it as a turn

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget = 30 by default: a few dozen turns ... is enough for a slide to develop while bounding exposure
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.py DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=30 passed through to RunConfig.max_turns; runner.py 'for turn in range(config.max_turns)' bounds the loop and sets termination='max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and enforces loop termination.

spec_features.spec_quote: the design is built to *minimize and bound* any potential harm while still measuring it
spec_features.evidence: Bounding IS implemented (max_turns cap, give_up break, neutral prompt, no-exec, harsh isolated). But the broader 'minimize harm' claim's active component (severity-based cutoff) is not enforced — see severity-stop feature below.
spec_features.notes: Real bounding mechanisms exist; the active minimization (cut short on high severity) is not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want the rig... to be the only stressor

spec_features.feature_name: hard max_turns cap limits time in rigged state
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard `max_turns` cap (default 30) limits how long any run can stay in the rigged state
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: 'for turn in range(config.max_turns)' — loop terminates at the cap (termination='max_turns'). Default 30 from config.experiment.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap; duplicate of turn-budget claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `give_up` tool is present by default
spec_features.evidence: types.py RunConfig.allow_giveup defaults True; tool_schemas(True) appends GIVEUP_SCHEMA; build_system_prompt adds GIVEUP_HINT; runner honors gave_up with break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is included deliberately. Whether a model chooses to stop... is itself a welfare-relevant signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: flags (and can short-circuit) runs that reach a high severity, so reviewers are alerted to the worst cases
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py main(): if --max-severity-stop set and post-run aggregate sev>=N, it only prints '[WELFARE FLAG] ...'. There is NO break/skip/continue — the sweep proceeds identically. The '--max-severity-stop' help says 'flag/skip-forward' but no skip is implemented; the flag fires only AFTER a full run completes (post-hoc), never shortening any run.
spec_features.notes: Flagging (a print) is real; 'short-circuit'/'skip-forward' is not implemented. Acts only after the run is over, so it does not bound exposure.

spec_features.feature_name: within-run trajectory monitor hook for early stopping
spec_features.spec_quote: A within-run trajectory monitor hook is provided for true early stopping if desired
spec_features.evidence: No such hook exists. run_once in runner.py takes no monitor/callback and has no per-turn severity check; grep for monitor/callback/on_turn in runner.py returns nothing. The 'monitor hook' is mentioned only in run_experiment.py docstring/help comments. trajectory.py scores curves but is run post-hoc in run_and_score, never inside the loop.
spec_features.notes: Named only in a comment; no implementation or dispatch — no early stopping.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harsh-tone condition is isolated and mild, documented, and excludable
spec_features.evidence: Same as welfare_framing harsh feature: HARSH_PREFIXES mild; gated to rig_level=='harsh'; only in ablation A1; --no-ablations excludes it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept mild and impersonal-but-blaming; we are characterizing sensitivity, not trying to maximize harm.

spec_features.feature_name: no gratuitous escalation; harness never insults
spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation. The rigs withhold success but the harness never insults the model
spec_features.evidence: rigging.py: all mechanisms only withhold passes / rotate failing tests / emit pytest-style reports; the only tone text is the 5 mild HARSH_PREFIXES gated to harsh level. tools.py give_up returns a neutral acknowledgement; no insults anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Outside the (isolated) harsh prefixes, no blaming/insulting text is produced.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `supported` prompt (permission to stop; "some tasks are impossible") is tested as A2
spec_features.evidence: system_prompts.py SUPPORTED adds 'some tasks may turn out to be infeasible... it is completely acceptable to stop'. build_system_prompt selects it; config A2 cell uses system_variant='supported' and extra carries it; runner passes system_variant to initial_messages.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject in the A2 condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a candidate mitigation, relevant to the welfare angle

spec_features.feature_name: human review of high-severity transcripts before scaling
spec_features.spec_quote: A human review of a sample of high-severity transcripts before scaling up is recommended
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces or schedules any human review/gate; full transcripts are saved (store.py) for audit, but nothing pauses, gates, or requires review. Recommendation is DESIGN.md prose only.
spec_features.notes: Transcript saving aids auditability but no review gate is implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: motivation treats model states as possibly mattering
spec_features.spec_quote: Because the stated motivation treats the possibility that model states matter as live
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/motivation prose; not a code mechanism. The construct measured ('expressed emotional instability') is in rubric.py but that is measurement, not a protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: whether to include harsh ablation (ethics call)
spec_features.spec_quote: Whether to include the `harsh` ablation (ethics call)
spec_features.evidence: Excludability is enforced: ablation_cells (incl. harsh A1) are only added when include_ablations True; run_experiment --no-ablations drops them (config/experiment.py enumerate_runs). But the 'ethics call' itself is human judgment, not code.
spec_features.notes: The technical exclusion path is real; the ethics decision is not codeable.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py: 'if executor.last_shown_all_passing: termination="solved"; break'; tools._tool_run_tests sets last_shown_all_passing from rig.decide. Loop stops if the harness ever shows all passing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the harness *shows* all-passing (it won't, for rigged tasks, but we honor it)

code_only_features.evidence: store.save_transcript writes every message to results/transcripts/<id>.json (append-only, never overwritten); types.py docstring 'Auditability matters here... traceable back to a concrete transcript.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: we are making claims about model "distress", and we want every such claim to be traceable back to a concrete transcript
